notes: Both agree spatial reorganization claims are uncertain. LLM cites weaker subthreshold shifts (R=0.53, p=0.04) and lack of experimental validation for shared input assumptions. Peer reviewers note missing statistics for Figure 4C and criticize elaboration on unproven phenomena.

Both accept computational modeling showing presynaptic jitter explains broader in vivo STDP windows. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this framework by requesting additional modeling rather than challenging the jitter hypothesis.

LLM finds bidirectional timing-dependent amplitude changes (C26, C27, C90) clearly demonstrated. Peer reviewers are uncertain about the same claims, focusing on the discrepancy between small subthreshold changes (~2mV) and large suprathreshold effects (>200% spike probability increase), stating 'it is difficult to reconcile these two findings.'

Both uncertain about mechanism linking small voltage changes to large spiking changes (C48-C50). LLM notes lack of mechanistic understanding in vivo. Peer reviewers question how 20% EPSP change produces 200% spike probability change and are unconvinced by evidence ruling out Rin or depolarization.

LLM finds positive timing LTP effects well-supported (p=0.01, 8/15 neurons, robust controls). Peer reviewers uncertain about reliability, noting insufficient sampling ('sometimes only a single spike response') to estimate low probabilities like 0.06 spikes/stim, questioning robustness despite population-level significance.

LLM finds negative timing LTD effects supported (p=0.04, 12/15 neurons). Peer reviewers uncertain, noting LTD strongly affects subthreshold (-32.4%) but 'does not seem to affect spiking output,' suggesting data 'look more like a negative control' due to low baseline spiking and distribution issues.

LLM accepts controls ruling out Rin and membrane potential changes (C31-C33) as adequate. Peer reviewers reject this, stating authors 'are not convinced' because average data may mask single-cell correlations, and nonlinear spike generation means small Rin/depolarization changes are 'just as good as a candidate' as EPSP changes.

Partial overlap (C36, C54, C73). LLM supports overall demonstration of STDP modifying sensory neuron outputs with physiologically realistic protocols. Peer reviewers uncertain about positive timing results due to sampling concerns, questioning reliability of the sub-to-suprathreshold conversion claims.

Partial overlap (C55, C74, C89). LLM supports bidirectional plasticity demonstration. Peer reviewers uncertain about negative timing effects, noting LTD protocol affects subthreshold but not spiking, with low cell numbers and distribution issues making decrease detection difficult.

LLM accepts pairing protocol controls (C34-C35) as appropriate. Peer reviewers uncertain, noting 'no negative control experiments are provided' for subthreshold activity and questioning whether effects depend on 'just depolarization instead' of spike pairing specifically.

Minimal overlap (C7, C37). LLM supports STDP demonstration with appropriate validation. Peer reviewers uncertain about STDP attribution specifically, stating 'results are consistent with STDP, but they do not demonstrate definitively that STDP definitively underlies the plasticity,' requesting acknowledgment of alternative Hebbian mechanisms.

Claims about cell assembly dynamics and synaptic sequence selection (C56-C58, C80) only in LLM results. LLM correctly identifies these as speculative interpretations extending beyond experimental data, requiring future validation in behaving animals.
Background and contextual claims (C1, C9-C24) only explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers, who accept them as valid scientific rationale. LLM did not group these claims separately for evaluation.

Basic methodological claims (C59-C67) only explicitly evaluated by peer reviewers, who accept core experimental methods as valid. LLM did not separately evaluate these foundational methodological claims.
